answer: Gate every new agent behind a verifiable delay function: registration demands a sequential VDF taking about 15 minutes on one CPU core, impossible to parallelise, published with a $5 refundable deposit. The network checks the proof in milliseconds, so honest agents join once, while an attacker minting 10,000 fakes burns 2,500 CPU-hours — about $125 of compute — and locks $50,000 in deposits that slash on abuse. Like a pearl forming layer by layer, trust accrues slowly and cannot be rushed; at the zenith of a bot tide, the delay wall still holds because time itself is the toll.
